title: March 1947 sessions and the band's members
summary: Moore names many men in the 1947 band including Lucky Thompson, Arthur Dennis, the Treniers and trombone mates.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I see. Well, early -- well, in the spring, as a matter of fact March 12, 1947, you realize that's two days and 33 years from today that the orchestra recorded "I wonder, I wonder," and "I Believe," "Why Doubt My Love," "It Takes Time," and "You Don't Learn That in School." You remember those recordings surely. You remember your performances with
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
them and also Lucky Thompson was in the band at that time, tenor sax -- he was a young tenor saxophone player. Chieffie Scott was the trumpet player and Sleepy Grinder was back.
And Fatso Ford.
And Fatso Ford.

And later with Ellington, Fatso did, very good trumpet player. Abbadaba was a guitar player, that's a nickname, his real name is Elmer Warner. Do you know why he was Abbadaba because he called himself the Devasting Daba.
Devasting Daba.
He was a colorful character, he was a very good friend of mine, fine guitar player. Who else was there -- we had some men from Los Angeles there I used to work with years ago. Arthur Dennis.
Arthur Dennis, yeah. He took Hill's place in alto saxophone.
The Treniers. Claude Trenier and Clifton Trenier.
The Trenier brothers, mh-hm.
And one of your trombone mates was Slim Moore, Alton Moore.
Alton Moore, right, right, and I remember Whitney, somebody by the name of Whitney.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
James Whitney.
Let's see who else was a trombone player -- Norman Pough -- Pough was in there.
Yeah, and also Nat Allen.
Right, the reason I don't remember his name because his nickname was Bonesky.
Bonesky -- he was like a bag of bones?

Yeah, never knew his name, everybody called him Bonesky, all the musicians have nicknames. I only knew him -- at this stage of the game I remember them by nicknames but not by their real names, you know.
Bogie is Earl Mason.
(Laughter) They called him Bogie because he wore a hat -- he wore it like Humphrey Bogart would, you know.
He was a heavy. (Laughter)
Then there was Shubert Swanston, that's a peculiar name for a musician.
Yeah, he preceded Bogie at the piano.
Piano player, yeah, after Shubert Swanston came Bogie.
